summary: Defines the value "application" for the vCard KIND property so a vCard can represent a software application. A contact card can describe a program as well as a person or organization.

plainLanguage.summary: A contact card usually lists a person. This lets a contact card describe a program instead, like a note for an app in your address book.

questions: how to represent software in vcard
subtitle: Adds an 'application' value to the vCard KIND property so a vCard can describe software.

tldr.problem: The vCard KIND property had no value for software applications such as servers, chat rooms or bots.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6473 defines KIND value 'application' and discusses which vCard properties apply.
tldr.outcome: vCards can describe software, as already done for instant messaging servers in XMPP.

today: RFC 6473 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no replacement or update.

sections.title: A New KIND Value
sections.content: vCard version 4 (RFC 6350) has a KIND property with the values individual, organization, group and location. The working group removed a generic "thing" value, expecting an extension might define one. This document defines a narrower application value instead.
sections.plainLanguage: Contact cards had kinds like person and place. This adds 'program'.

sections.title: What application Means
sections.content:
The vCard represents a software application such as a server, an online service (for example a chat room) or an automated software bot. It is functionally equivalent to the LDAP applicationProcess object class. vCards are already used in XMPP (RFC 6120) to represent instant messaging servers.

Properties may describe the application itself, the organization or person making it available, or the person or role maintaining it. For the application itself, the work and home TYPE values make no sense. Properties such as ADR, EMAIL, FN, GEO, IMPP, KEY, LOGO, TEL, TZ and URL make sense. A finer taxonomy is out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: The card can list the program's name, website and who to contact, but a program has no home or office.

sections.title: Example and IANA
sections.content:
The example, borrowed from XEP-0292, is the XML form (RFC 6351) of a vCard for a jabber.org IM service with <kind><text>application</text></kind>. IANA added application to the registry of vCard4 property values, for use with KIND.

No security considerations are expected beyond those for vCards in general.
sections.plainLanguage: The example is a card for a chat service, with its name, website and email.
